summary: Natalie Maxwell is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under doctoral supervisor Stephan V. Beyer, also studying under Ngawang Wangyal, Khensur Ngawang Legden, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Minoru Kiyota.
Natalie Rothman is a historian who studied at the University of Michigan from 1999 to 2006. In 2006, she held a post at the University of Toronto.

Natasha Heller specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies, earning her PhD from Harvard University in 2005. She was a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellow at UC Berkeley (attested 2008) and an assistant professor at UCLA (attested 2016).

Natasha Reichle, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, completed her dissertation at the University of California, Berkeley under Joanna Gottfried Williams. She also studied under Amin Sweeney, Lewis Lancaster, Patricia Berger, Jeffrey Hadler, and Ninik Lunde.
Natasja Bosma is an Indology scholar who earned her PhD under Hans T. Bakker at the University of Groningen between circa 2012 and 2018, where she also held an academic post during the same period.

Nathan Sivin was a Sinologist and historian of science who studied at MIT, Kyoto University, and Harvard (PhD circa 1960–1966). He held faculty posts at MIT (1966–1977) and the University of Pennsylvania (1977–2006).

Nathan W. Hill, a scholar of linguistics, Tibetology, and Sinology, studied at Harvard University. He was a reader at SOAS (circa 2008–2019) and became Sam Lam Professor in Chinese Studies at Trinity College Dublin in 2021.
Nathaniel Brassey Halhed was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Harrow School and Christ Church, Oxford. He served as an official for the East India Company from circa 1771 to 1785.

Nathaniel DeWitt Garson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under doctoral supervisor Jeffrey Hopkins, and also studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Namdrol.
Nathaniel Wallich studied at the University of Copenhagen. He served as Superintendent of the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden from circa 1817 to 1846.

Nathmal Tatia was an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned a Doctor of Literature at the University of Calcutta under Satkari Mookerjee. He served as Director of the Jain Vishva Bharati Institute (attested 1982–1990).
Navina Lamminger is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of Munich under doctoral supervisor Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Nawang Tsering Shakspo is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under doctoral supervisor Lal Mani Joshi. He served as a lecturer at the Central Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1985).
Neal Donner is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at the University of British Columbia, where he was taught by Leon Hurvitz (attested 1976).

Nenghai Shi was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Peking University and under teachers including Kecheng Zhang and Khangsar Dorje Chang. He served as vice-president of the Buddhist Association of China from 1953 to 1966.

Newton Mohun Dutt worked in the field of Indology and served as Curator of Libraries for Baroda State, the Central Library of Baroda, and the Baroda State Department of Archaeology from circa 1922 to 1935.
Ng-Fung Yuen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of the West under doctoral supervisor Kottegoda Warnasuriya (attested 2009).
Ngak Sé Rigpé Dorjé studied under Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok and Khenpo Tsultrim Lodro.
Ngakchang Gönpo Tsé Ten studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Ngan-che Chan is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Jing Yin (attested 2007), also studying under K. L. Dhammajoti.
